text.p: Following are the main stories in Thursday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Several passports and travel documents were stolen from the Immigration Department in the northern Malaysian town of Ipoh.
-- Asean foreign ministers will take a united stand to stop extraneous issues from being dragged into the their talks with the European Union in Singapore, they said.
-- The soon-to-be-launched Dana Mutiara closed end fund will concentrate on infrastructure development projects in Penang.
-- Government departments remained almost empty with most civil servants still on leave after the five-day, Chinese and Moslem double holiday.
-- Land will have to be set aside to build social and religious facilities for all communities, said Abdul Rahman Abdullah, chief executive of the Construction Industry Development Board.

-- Transwater Corp Bhd is set to undergo a restructuring exercise that will see it being divided into four main business areas, with the possibility of a fifth being incorporated into the structure, said its chairman Wan Adli Wan Ibrahim.
